title: Airbnb Automated Messages Setup and 8 Templates (2026)
summary: How Airbnb's scheduled quick replies work in 2026, the details (shortcodes) you can use, 8 message templates to copy, and what native automation can't do.
body_markdown:
Airbnb's automated messages are called scheduled quick replies. You write a template once, choose the listings it covers and when it goes out (after booking, before or after check-in, before or after checkout), and Airbnb sends it for each reservation on those listings. On May 20, 2026 Airbnb also announced Auto-replies, which use AI to answer common guest questions from your listing, and said they would roll out over the following months.


I checked every feature on this page against Airbnb's Help Center and Resource Center on November 26, 2026. Where Airbnb doesn't document something, the page says so.


## What automated messaging tools does Airbnb give hosts?


Airbnb gives hosts six messaging and check-in tools inside the inbox and listing editor. Four reach the guest without you doing anything per booking, though only scheduled quick replies and Auto-replies post in the message thread; connected smart lock codes arrive by email and in the guest's Trips tab. The other two save typing when you answer a guest yourself.


Tool What it does Reaches the guest without you? Where to set it up


[Scheduled quick replies](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2897) Posts your template in the thread before or after booking, check-in or checkout Yes Messages > Settings > Manage quick replies


[Quick replies](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2898) Saved templates you insert into a conversation No Messages > Settings > Manage quick replies


[Suggested quick replies](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2898) AI suggests one of your existing quick replies for a guest's question No, you choose to send Appears in the conversation


[Auto-replies](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/respond-faster-in-the-messages-tab-770) AI answers common questions from your amenities, description and house manual, with Airbnb named as the sender Yes, per Airbnb's May 2026 announcement; no Help Center article yet Not documented


[Connected smart lock codes](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3483) Unique 4-digit code per guest in the confirmation email, reminder emails 8 and 2 days before check-in, and the Trips tab Yes Smart lock connection in Airbnb


[Check-in instructions](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1926) Guests see the method at booking and the detailed steps 48 hours before check-in Yes Listing editor > Arrival guide


## How do you set up scheduled messages on Airbnb?


You set up scheduled quick replies in the Messages tab. Each template applies to current and upcoming reservations on the listings you pick, and Airbnb sends it in each listing's time zone ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2897) ). On desktop it takes seven steps, and the same template can then run on every listing you host.


1. Click Messages, then Settings.
2. Click Manage quick replies, then Create.
3. If you have several listings, choose the hosting type.
4. Name the template and write the message, inserting details (Airbnb's word for shortcodes).
5. Click Choose listings and select the listings it applies to.
6. Click Scheduled for and pick the timing.
7. Click Save.


Before you save, decide on the toggle labeled "Send for last minute bookings and short stays." With it off, Airbnb skips messages that can't go out as scheduled: a message set for 2 days before check-in on a booking made the same day, or a message set for 2 days before checkout on a 1-night stay. With it on, messages timed before check-in go out at the moment of booking, and any other message that would have been skipped goes out at the check-in time set for the listing. Airbnb sends you a notification and an email when a message is skipped or sent at an unscheduled time.


To change a single reservation without touching the template, open the guest's thread, click Add+, then View scheduled quick replies. The timeline lets you edit, skip or send any upcoming message early. Deleting a template removes every unsent message it scheduled across all its listings, so use Skip when you only want to stop one.


On a hosting team, members with guest management permissions share one set of scheduled quick replies, and every message is sent from the team owner. A co-host can see the sent and upcoming scheduled messages in each conversation, skip or edit them, and apply their own templates to your listing, but can't view or edit your templates, because Airbnb doesn't share quick replies between hosts and co-hosts.


## Which shortcodes (details) can you use in Airbnb messages?


Details fill in guest, reservation and listing information each time a message is sent. The examples in[Airbnb's help article](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2897) name guest first name, check-in date, check-in time, checkout date, checkout time, address, directions, wifi name, wifi password, house rules, city and confirmation code. Airbnb does not publish a complete list.


A detail pulls from your listing, so if the field is empty (including some optional fields) the guest sees the detail marked as unavailable. Fill in address, directions, wifi and house rules on every listing before you switch a template on. With a connected smart lock you can also use an entry code detail, which inserts each guest's own code ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3483) ).


Each message is limited to 4,000 characters, so split anything longer into two templates ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2898) ). Airbnb translates messages into the guest's language, and the language set on the template affects how the details are translated.


## What should your Airbnb message templates say?


Eight Airbnb message templates cover a normal stay: six scheduled quick replies from booking to after checkout, and two manual quick replies for early check-in and late checkout requests. Words in \[brackets\] are Airbnb details; replace anything in plain capitals with your own text. Leave outside links out, because Airbnb does not allow "links in listing pages or messages that take people off of the Airbnb platform" ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2799) ).


Checkout wording has a newer limit. For reservations booked on or after November 20, 2026, Airbnb's[house rules policy](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/4168) says hosts may not communicate new house rules after booking, including by message, and generally may not ask guests to strip the bed, take trash off-site, or wash and put away dishes. Any checkout step in template 5 should already be in your listing's house rules.


### 1. Booking confirmed


Schedule: shortly after booking. The second paragraph assumes the last-minute toggle is on in template 2.


> Hi \[guest first name\], thanks for booking. You're confirmed for \[check-in date\] to \[checkout date\], confirmation code \[confirmation code\].
>
>
> Check-in is from \[check-in time\] and checkout is by \[checkout time\]. Directions and wifi details come in a separate message 3 days before you arrive, or right away if you booked closer to the date than that. Ask me here about the area or the house.


### 2. Three days before check-in


Schedule: 3 days before check-in.


> Hi \[guest first name\], your stay starts on \[check-in date\]. Here's what you need for arrival.
>
>
> Address: \[address\] Directions: \[directions\] Parking: PARKING INSTRUCTIONS Wifi: \[wifi name\], password \[wifi password\]
>
>
> House rules: \[house rules\]
>
>
> If your arrival time changes, let me know here.


### 3. Check-in day, with access


Schedule: morning of check-in. With a connected smart lock, Airbnb has already emailed the code at booking and 8 and 2 days out, so this message puts it in the thread on the day the guest needs it. Without one, replace the code line with your lockbox or keypad steps.


> Hi \[guest first name\], the place is ready for you from \[check-in time\] today at \[address\].
>
>
> Your door code is \[entry code\]. It starts working at check-in time.
>
>
> Wifi: \[wifi name\], password \[wifi password\]
>
>
> If you have any trouble getting in, message me here and I'll help.


### 4. Morning after the first night


Schedule: the day after check-in, mid-morning. On a 1-night stay this lands on checkout morning, so skip it in that reservation's timeline.


> Good morning \[guest first name\]. I hope the first night went well. If anything isn't working or you're missing something, tell me here and I'll sort it out.


### 5. Checkout reminder


Schedule: morning of the day before checkout. On a 1-night stay that time falls before check-in: with the toggle off Airbnb skips the message, and with it on the message goes out at check-in time, when "checkout is tomorrow" is still true.


> Hi \[guest first name\], a reminder that checkout is tomorrow, \[checkout date\], by \[checkout time\].
>
>
> Before you go: CHECKOUT STEPS FROM YOUR HOUSE RULES (for example, put used dishes in the sink, gather used towels, lock the door).
>
>
> If you'd like to leave later, ask me today and I'll check whether the cleaning schedule allows it.


### 6. After checkout: thank you and review request


Schedule: a few hours after checkout.


> Hi \[guest first name\], thank you for staying with us. I hope the trip home is easy.
>
>
> If you have a minute, a review on Airbnb helps the next guests know what to expect. I'll be reviewing your stay too. You're welcome back any time you're in \[city\].


### 7. Early check-in request (manual quick reply)


Send when a guest asks to arrive early. If the guest wants to arrive a day early, that is an added night, and Airbnb requires its Change reservation tool to collect payment for it ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2799) ).


> Hi \[guest first name\], standard check-in is \[check-in time\] so the cleaners have time to reset the place. I'll check the schedule for \[check-in date\] and reply here as soon as I know whether you can come in earlier.


### 8. Late checkout request (manual quick reply)


Send when a guest asks to leave after checkout time.


> Hi \[guest first name\], standard checkout is \[checkout time\] on \[checkout date\]. Let me check whether anyone arrives that day and get back to you here about a later time.


For review wording after the stay, see these[Airbnb host review templates](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/20-airbnb-host-review-templates-and-automated-workflows) .


## Why do guests still ask questions you already answered?


Across a year of guest messages (about 10 million, August 2025 to July 2026), Conduit found that 27.4% of guests who asked for the door code had already been sent it, unprompted, earlier in the same thread ([full analysis](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/what-10-million-guest-messages-are-about) ). The figure was 20.8% for check-in time and 18.4% for the wifi password, and 908,000 threads had received a full templated pre-arrival message. Those numbers count only information typed into a message, so guidebook links and PDFs are not included.


A guest reads the 3-day message while planning the trip, and needs the code later, at the door. Put the access details in the check-in-day message as well (template 3), and keep a manual quick reply ready for each of the three questions so you can answer right away when someone asks anyway.


## What can't Airbnb's scheduled messages do?


Airbnb's scheduled quick replies send fixed text at a fixed time to each reservation on the listings you chose. Five gaps show up once you host more than a few listings or take bookings from Vrbo, Booking.com or your own website. Each gap below means a person steps in, or a second tool does the job.


1. They don't read the guest's message. A question about a crib or a late arrival still needs a person to answer it. Airbnb's Auto-replies are meant to cover common questions, but only with what is already written on your listing, and each reply names Airbnb as the sender. You can delete one and send your own answer.
2. Airbnb documents no trigger for a changed or canceled reservation, and doesn't say what happens to queued messages when dates move. After a change, open the timeline and check what is still scheduled.
3. Airbnb's help article lists no stay-length or guest-count condition, so one template goes to a 1-night stay and a 14-night stay alike.
4. They only cover Airbnb, so guests who booked elsewhere need a separate setup.
5. They can't act anywhere else. A scheduled message can't move a cleaning or create a code on a lock that isn't connected to Airbnb.


## When should a PMS or AI agent take over?


A property management system (PMS) should run your messaging as soon as you list on a second booking site, because Airbnb's scheduled quick replies never reach a Vrbo or Booking.com guest. An AI agent is worth adding when most of your inbox time goes to free-form questions and the tasks that follow them. If you host a few listings and every booking comes through Airbnb, scheduled quick replies plus a set of manual quick replies cover the whole stay.


In a PMS you write the arrival sequence once per property, and it goes to the Airbnb guest and the Vrbo guest alike. If you also list on Vrbo, the setup there is covered in[Vrbo automated messages](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/vrbo-automated-messages) . With an AI agent connected, a guest who writes that the dryer has stopped gets a reply with what to try, and a maintenance task opens in your PMS. For a side-by-side of the software hosts use for this, see[Airbnb automation tools](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/airbnb-automation-tools) .


Conduit is an AI agent of that kind for Airbnb hosts, connected to your PMS and task tools. See how it works for[Airbnb messaging](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/short-term-rentals/airbnb-messaging) .


## FAQ


Two things changed for Airbnb message templates in 2026. Airbnb announced Auto-replies in May but has no Help Center article on them, and its house rules policy for reservations booked from November 20 limits what a checkout reminder may ask. Setup, short stays, response rate and door codes are the other common questions.


### How do I set up automated messages on Airbnb?


Open Messages, then Settings, then Manage quick replies, and click Create. Write the template, pick the listings and a send time under Scheduled for, decide on the last-minute toggle, and save.


### Do scheduled quick replies reach guests who booked before I made the template?


Yes. A new scheduled quick reply applies to current and upcoming reservations on the listings you pick, and each message goes out in that listing's time zone.


### Do Airbnb automated messages help my response rate?


Response rate counts the new inquiries and reservation requests you answer within 24 hours over the past 30 days. Scheduled quick replies are timed from bookings, check-in and checkout, so a pending reservation request still needs you to accept or decline it. Airbnb does not say whether an Auto-reply counts as your response.


### How should I handle 1-night stays with scheduled messages?


Turn on the last-minute toggle in each template, so a message that would land before check-in goes out at the listing's check-in time instead of being skipped. For a message that makes no sense on a short stay, such as a morning-after check-in, skip it in that reservation's timeline.


### Can I turn off Airbnb's Auto-replies?


Airbnb has not documented a way to turn Auto-replies off. Its May 2026 announcement says each one names Airbnb as the sender, that you can delete it and send your own answer, and that answers come from your amenities, listing description and house manual, so keep those sections accurate.


### Can an automated message remind guests of checkout chores?


Only for chores already in your listing's house rules. For reservations booked on or after November 20, 2026, Airbnb says hosts cannot add house rules after booking, including by message, and generally cannot ask guests to strip beds, take trash off-site, or wash and put away dishes.


### Does Airbnb already send guests the door code?


With a connected smart lock, yes. Each guest gets a unique code in the confirmation email, in reminder emails 8 and 2 days before check-in and in the Trips tab, and the code works from check-in time until checkout. Without a connected lock, the code has to go in your own message or check-in instructions.
